purpose: Rebuild the pinned PostgreSQL 18.6 source with --with-openssl --with-icu --with-readline --with-zlib, enable scram-sha-256 password auth and loopback TLS, and rerun the application acceptance against it, narrowing open_gaps[hosting-services][9] ('accepted database configuration uses loopback and local trust and omits TLS, ICU, readline and zlib; does not qualify a production database profile').
preregistered: If configure accepts all four flags, the build links against openssl/icu/readline/zlib (verified via ldd and via `initdb --locale-provider=icu` succeeding), TLS negotiates and non-TLS connections are rejected by pg_hba, and the app's 12 API/DB tests pass against this database, that settles the gap as executed evidence toward a materially less minimal database profile (still not a full production install: no PAM/GSSAPI/LDAP, still loopback-only, still a synthetic fixture). Any configure/build/link failure, or TLS/scram not actually enforced (e.g. a non-TLS connection succeeding), or the app tests failing against this database, would refute readiness and must be recorded verbatim, not worked around silently.

result: The pinned PostgreSQL 18.6 source rebuilds cleanly with --with-openssl --with-icu --with-readline --with-zlib once the extracted -dev packages' broken runtime symlinks are fixed (a build/link issue, not a design blocker), and the resulting binary genuinely links and uses openssl (ldd) and icu (initdb --locale-provider=icu succeeds). scram-sha-256 password auth and loopback TLS were both enabled and enforced: a non-TLS connection was rejected by pg_hba with FATAL, and this rejection is independently corroborated by the retained postgres-hardened.log server log (FATAL line present), not only by the summary transcript. The app's 12 pytest API/DB tests (the DB-layer subset of the application's full `make verify` acceptance sequence -- TypeScript checking, the production build and the one Playwright browser workflow were not rerun here) passed unchanged against this hardened database. This narrows open_gaps[9]: the previously 'omits TLS, ICU, readline and zlib' database profile is replaced, in this receipt's evidence, by a build and running instance with all four plus enforced scram+TLS, still on loopback and still a synthetic fixture (no PAM/GSSAPI/LDAP, no shared-user service, no production deployment claim).

verdict_impact.explanation: PostgreSQL remains the selected database; this receipt strengthens its hosting-services evidence by closing the specific 'omits TLS/ICU/readline/zlib' criticism with an executed, passing build and acceptance rerun, rather than changing the selection. It does not establish a production deployment, PAM/GSSAPI/LDAP auth, a shared-user service, or hosted/cloud operation, all of which remain out of scope per gap_index 1 (needs_paid_entitlement) and gap_index 8 (needs_hardware).

limitations: Loopback-only (127.0.0.1), synthetic trust-free fixture; still not a production database installation or shared-user service.
No PAM, GSSAPI, LDAP, or SELinux support was configured or tested; only openssl/icu/readline/zlib were added, matching the exact gap text.
The self-signed certificate is a locally generated fixture cert, not from any CA; suitable only for this loopback acceptance.

The extracted -dev packages' runtime .so symlinks had to be manually repaired by copying already-installed system runtime libraries; this is a workable but nonstandard install path compared to a true `apt install` with root, and would not reproduce identically on a host lacking those exact runtime package versions already installed.

Build/link took several iterations to resolve (missing pkg-config -> ICU_CFLAGS/ICU_LIBS override; missing bison/flex/m4 -> extracted and added to PATH; ICU C++ link failures -> fixed by repairing dev-symlinks rather than by adding -lstdc++, which alone was insufficient) before reaching the single final passing configure/build/install run reported above; only the final, passing sequence is treated as the settled result.

This receipt reran only the 12 pytest API/database tests, not the application's full `make verify` acceptance sequence (peer checks, API/schema/generated-type drift checks, TypeScript checking, the production build and one Playwright browser workflow per blueprints/convergence-practice/application-delivery/README.md); Next.js/React were not built or started here, so the pytest pass does not itself establish frontend acceptance against this hardened database.

The raw_artifacts transcript (gap9-hardened-postgres.txt) is a contemporaneous author-written summary produced after the command sequence completed, not a captured verbatim terminal transcript; several commands' output_excerpt text above is drawn from that summary rather than an isolated raw capture.
